newsitem.title: USA: CFTC says reform means "profound impact" on farmer.
newsitem.headline: CFTC says reform means "profound impact" on farmer.

text.p: Commodity Futures Trading Commission chairwoman Brooksley Born said Thursday that pending legislation to strip the agency of much of its jurisdiction over large traders could impact farmers and ranchers trying to use futures to protect their crop investments.
The proposed legislation, pending before both the House and Senate, could have a "profound impact" on farmers and other hedgers, she said.

The bill would eliminate regulation of the futures exchanges "at the very time that the risk management responsibilities embodied in the Federal Agricultural Improvement and Reform Act have made farmers and ranchers more dependent on futures markets than ever before," Born said in testimony before a House Agriculture subcommittee.

In a series of Hill appearances and speeches in recent weeks, Born has criticized the proposed legislation as stripping the CFTC of the tools it needs to prevent and detect fraud and manipulation in the futures and options market.

The CFTC and the U.S. Agriculture Department have formed a group to educate farmers and ranchers about risk management tools they can use to protect their crops. The tools include traditional futures, as well as crop revenue or yield insurance, forward contracts and other instruments.
The biggest U.S. futures exchanges have pressed Congress to rein in the CFTC's powers, saying the agency's paperwork and regulatory requirements make U.S. exchanges uncompetitive in a global market.
